one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration platform with channels, DMs, and an extensive app/bot ecosystem.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can create apps and generate OAuth tokens instantly at api.slack.com/apps; public distribution/marketplace listing requires a separate app review, but building and using an app in your own workspace is immediate.
api_surface: Broad REST Web API (chat, channels, users, files, canvases) plus Events API, Socket Mode, and RTM; hundreds of methods across dozens of scopes.
existing_mcp_detail: Slack has an official MCP server enabling assistants like Claude/Perplexity to search and act in Slack; community servers like korotovsky/slack-mcp-server also exist.
notes: OAuth scopes tightly govern access; public app distribution/marketplace listing requires Slack app review, but self-workspace integrations are frictionless.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform providing programmable SMS, voice, video, and verification APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can sign up for a free trial account instantly and get Account SID/Auth Token or create API keys via the Console without approval.
api_surface: Very broad REST API spanning Voice, Messaging (SMS/MMS/WhatsApp), Verify, phone number provisioning, SIP, and usage/account management.
existing_mcp_detail: Official twilio-labs/mcp monorepo (published as @twilio-alpha/mcp) exposes Twilio's API as MCP tools.
notes: Production use of phone numbers/messaging may require A2P 10DLC registration depending on country, but core API access itself is immediately self-serve with a trial account.

one_liner: Business team-chat and collaboration app from Zoho with bots, channels, and messaging APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers register apps in the Zoho API Console and complete the OAuth2 authorization-code flow themselves without manual approval for standard scopes.
api_surface: REST API v2/v3 covering channels, messages, chats, bots, and webhooks; moderate breadth, well documented.
existing_mcp_detail: Zoho publishes an official Cliq MCP server supporting Claude, Cursor, VS, Windsurf clients for messaging/reminders/channel management.
notes: Access tokens expire hourly requiring refresh-token handling.

one_liner: All-in-one enterprise collaboration suite (chat, docs, calendar, base) from ByteDance with an open platform API.
self_serve_evidence: Developers can register a custom app on open.larksuite.com and obtain App ID/App Secret (tenant token) or run OAuth2 for user tokens without needing manual approval for internal/custom apps.
api_surface: Extensive Server API (REST, tenant_access_token / user_access_token) covering messaging, docs, calendar, approval, contacts, and more across the whole Lark/Feishu suite.
existing_mcp_detail: Official larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp (published as @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp) wraps the Open Platform API as MCP tools.
notes: Publishing an app for external/public distribution goes through app review; internal/custom app development is immediate.

one_liner: Free team chat app (Slack alternative) from CAKE.com with channels, DMs, and workflow integrations.
self_serve_evidence: Any workspace member can generate an API key themselves via the built-in '/api-keys generate' slash command or the API Keys addon, no approval needed.
api_surface: Moderate REST API (via the 'API Keys' addon/Swagger docs) covering sending messages, replies, reactions, message deletion, channel creation/listing, and DMs; rate-limited to 1000 req/min per user.
existing_mcp_detail: Community MCP servers exist; no official Pumble/CAKE.com MCP found.
notes: API is delivered as an 'addon' (CAKE.com marketplace) rather than a first-class top-level API product.

one_liner: Voice, video, and text chat platform originally built for gaming communities, now widely used for community/team communication.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can create an application and bot in the Discord Developer Portal instantly, generate a bot token, and start calling the API with no approval step for standard bot scopes.
api_surface: Broad HTTP REST API plus a real-time Gateway (WebSocket) covering messages, channels, guilds, interactions (slash commands, components, modals), and monetization.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers; no official Discord-maintained MCP server was found.
notes: Bots requiring 'privileged intents' or verification at 100+ servers require Discord approval; small-scale/dev use is fully self-serve.

one_liner: Cloud-based messaging app with a public Bot API for building chatbots and automations.
self_serve_evidence: Anyone can create a bot instantly by messaging @BotFather to receive an auth token, no application review or approval required.
api_surface: Comprehensive Bot API covering messages, media, inline queries, polls, payments, business features, and chat/admin management; separate lower-level MTProto client API also exists.
existing_mcp_detail: Several community MCP servers exist; no official Telegram-maintained MCP server found.
notes: Bot API is distinct from the raw MTProto/user Client API; Bot API itself is fully sanctioned self-serve.

one_liner: Meta's business messaging API (Cloud API) enabling companies to send/receive WhatsApp messages at scale.
self_serve_evidence: Initial testing (temporary tokens, test numbers) can be set up self-serve via the Meta App Dashboard, but production use requires a permanent System User token, a connected WhatsApp Business Account, and Meta Business/App verification plus phone number display-name approval before scaling beyond limited messaging tiers.
api_surface: REST-based Graph API for sending template/session messages, receiving webhooks, media, and (newer) group/calling features; broad but tightly governed by messaging policies and conversation-based pricing.
existing_mcp_detail: Multiple community MCP servers wrap the official Cloud API; Meta has not published an official MCP server.
blocker: Meta Business verification and permanent-token/System-User setup gate production access; unverified businesses are capped on messaging volume and template approval.
notes: Sandbox/dev testing is quick and self-serve; the well-known friction is business verification, message template approval, and per-conversation pricing/rate tiers.

one_liner: Cloud-based business phone system and call center software with an API for calls, contacts, and messaging.
self_serve_evidence: Existing Aircall customers can self-serve generate api_id/api_token (Basic Auth) from Company Settings for their own account, but building a public multi-tenant integration requires OAuth2 credentials obtained only by applying to and being approved for Aircall's Tech Partner program.
api_surface: REST API (v1/v2) covering users, teams, calls, contacts, numbers, SMS/MMS/WhatsApp messaging, conversation intelligence (transcripts, sentiment), dialer campaigns, webhooks, and analytics; rate-limited to 120 req/min/company.
existing_mcp_detail: Unofficial community MCP server (73 tools) exists; no official Aircall-maintained MCP server found.
blocker: Public/OAuth-based integrations require approval into Aircall's Tech Partner program; single-account Basic Auth access is self-serve but not usable for a multi-tenant agent-toolkit product.
notes: For a toolkit meant to serve many customers, the Tech Partner approval requirement is the key friction; a single-workspace integration is otherwise straightforward via Basic Auth.

one_liner: Cloud communications platform (formerly Nexmo) offering programmable Voice, SMS, Verify, and Number Insight APIs.
self_serve_evidence: Developers sign up for an account and immediately receive an API key/secret from the Developer Dashboard or CLI, with free starting credit and no approval gate for core API access.
api_surface: Broad REST API portfolio covering Voice, SMS/Messages, Verify (2FA), Number Insight, and virtual number provisioning; JWT required for webhook-receiving APIs (e.g., Voice), Basic Auth/API key for simpler APIs like SMS.
existing_mcp_detail: Official Vonage-maintained MCP servers: Vonage-Community/telephony-mcp-server and Vonage/vonage-mcp-server-documentation.
notes: Some newer/regulated capabilities may need additional carrier or account-level enablement, but the core communications APIs are immediately self-serve.
